items.headline: Woman loses leg in Kangpokpi blast
items.text: A 41-year-old woman grazing cattle lost her left leg to a suspected explosive device, the area's third blast in about five days, villagers say. No police statement was reported.

photo.alt: Green paddy fields below forested hills under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: Paddy fields and hills around Kalapahar, Kangpokpi district, in 2021.

items.place: Nalkeri reserve forest, Nagarahole, Kodagu, Karnataka
items.headline: Karnataka seeks contempt against Nagarahole tribal families
items.text: Karnataka asked the High Court to hold 39 Jenu Kuruba families in contempt, saying they set up camps in a tiger reserve. A community group calls it "bureaucratic highhandedness".

photo.alt: Spotted deer walk between tall tree trunks in a misty forest.
photo.caption: Deer in the forest of Nagarahole, Karnataka, in 2011.

items.headline: Adivasi hamlets missing from power plant papers
items.text: Two Adivasi hamlets inside Adani Power's 2,400 MW plant site are absent from project documents; the ministry's EIA terms say "No R&R is involved". No company or official response was reported.

items.place: Kosmi village, Budhni, Sehore, Madhya Pradesh
items.headline: NHRC seeks report on Budhni tribal demolitions
items.text: The NHRC asked Sehore's collector for a report within a week on the demolition of tribal families' homes, crops and a well. No state response was reported.

items.headline: Police FIR over fake account-blocking notices
items.text: Delhi Police registered an FIR over forged police notices seeking to block the X accounts of digital-rights groups IFF and SFLC. A juvenile was traced to Srinagar, The Hindu reports.

items.headline: UNICEF: drones cause most child casualties in Sudan
items.text: Two in three child casualties in Sudan this year were caused by armed drones, UNICEF says; up to 15 power stations were hit in October. It could not say who launched them.

photo.alt: A wide view over a busy market with low roofs, vehicles and crowds.
photo.caption: The market in El Obeid, North Kordofan, in 2006.

items.place: Gaza City and Khan Younis, Gaza
items.headline: Father and son among eight killed in Gaza
items.text: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least eight Palestinians, including a 13-year-old boy and his father, local health sources said. No Israeli military comment was reported.

photo.alt: Multi-storey university buildings with arched windows above a leafy courtyard, with apartment towers behind.
photo.caption: The Luhaidan building and campus of the Islamic University of Gaza, Gaza City, in 2012, before the war.

items.headline: Settlers burn machinery at Beita industrial zone
items.text: The owner says over 150 settlers stoned workers and burned excavators. No army statement on Beita was reported; the army said it cleared four outposts elsewhere over repeated violence.

photo.alt: Parked cars on open ground below a hillside town of pale buildings.
photo.caption: Beita, south of Nablus, in 2020.

items.place: Nyaung Pin Lay, Kani Township, Sagaing, Myanmar
items.headline: Air strike on Sagaing school area kills 11
items.text: Residents say military gyrocopters bombed a school and homes on Saturday, killing 11 including four children; with no internet, a warning came too late. The military has not commented.

items.headline: UN: Egypt holds fact-checking site's whole newsroom
items.text: The UN rights office says Egypt detained all six Matsadash journalists; lawyers allege torture and forced confessions. It urged their release. No Egyptian response was reported.

photo.alt: A wide city street lined with tall older buildings, trees and parked cars.
photo.caption: Talaat Harb Street in central Cairo, in 2007.

items.headline: Police detain 154 after Yogyakarta protest clashes
items.text: A rally over wages and a protest ban ended in clashes at the regional council. Police say Molotov cocktails were thrown; legal aid group LBH reports 11 injured.

photo.alt: A city street with a green bus, motorbikes, a cycle rickshaw and a Jl. Malioboro sign.
photo.caption: Malioboro Street, Yogyakarta, in 2010.

items.headline: Privy Council strikes down Trinidad same-sex laws
items.text: The Privy Council ruled unanimously for activist Jason Jones that two sections criminalising consensual same-sex conduct are unconstitutional, dismissing the Attorney General's cross-appeal. A final order will follow.

focus.title: Sudan's long war
focus.dek: UNICEF says drones caused two in three child casualties in Sudan this year; up to 15 power stations were hit in October. Both sides deny targeting civilians.
